cards.text: Jesus has just finished telling a whole run of parables. Now He leaves that place and heads to His hometown. And friend, a hometown crowd is a WHOLE different kind of crowd.

cards.question: Back in His hometown, where does Jesus teach the people?
As Jesus teaches in their synagogue, the hometown people are ___.
Listening to Jesus in the synagogue, what are the hometown people asking?

answers.text: Where His wisdom and powers came from
When He will heal the sick in town
How long He plans to stay in town

cards.text: Then the crowd starts asking about everything they already know about Him. That's a hometown for you: I could show up renewed, edges sharp, standing on a gold base, and somebody would STILL say, "Hey, isn't that the old stamper from the back of the junk drawer?"

cards.question: The hometown crowd asks whether Jesus is the carpenter's son.
The hometown crowd says the name of Jesus's mother is ___.

cards.text: Then they ask about His brothers, one name after another: James, Joseph, Simon and Judas. Friend, they're flipping through His family photo album OUT LOUD, pointing at every face.

cards.question: The hometown crowd says all of Jesus's sisters are with them as well.

cards.text: And after all that, they land right back where they started: "Where then did this man get all these things?" They know His mother, His brothers, His sisters, and they STILL can't figure out where it came from.

cards.question: After all their questions, how do the people of His hometown treat Jesus?

answers.text: They ask Him to heal them

cards.text: Jesus doesn't give a speech. He answers them with one short line about a prophet and honor, and friend, that one line LANDS.

cards.question: According to Jesus, where is a prophet without honor?

answers.text: Only in his hometown and his own household
Only in big cities and royal courts

cards.question: In His hometown, Jesus did not do many ___ there, because of their ___.

findings.problem: Most of the stop's choices are discovery questions rather than informed guesses. Before cards 2, 3, 6, 7 and 9, the earlier cards give no basis for reasoning out the synagogue, the crowd's astonishment, the carpenter's-son question, Mary's name or whether Jesus's sisters are present. Five of nine choice cards therefore require prior knowledge or luck, which is more than the allowed few discovery questions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card retells that the crowd knows Jesus's mother and brothers, which comes from Matthew 13:55, as well as the sisters and repeated question in verse 56. Citing only Matthew 13:56 is too narrow for the material the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
